end.summary:
Practised levels of organisation: cell, tissue, organ, organ system, organism.
Used human examples including muscle tissue, heart, blood vessels, and circulatory system.
Compared tissue and organ: cells form tissues, and tissues form organs.
Yash ordered four levels correctly in one attempt; the organism step was unfinished.
The heart-versus-circulatory-system mix-up was revisited, but teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Asha practised the difference between tissues and organs, then built the sequence from cells to organ systems using human examples. Yash explained that cells form tissues and tissues form organs, and later recognised that the heart is one organ within the circulatory system; the earlier mix-up still needed a final clear explanation. At home, ask them to arrange five cards—cell, tissue, organ, organ system, organism—and give one human and one plant example for each.
